_sourceSlotAccounting: Twelve review source slots, each accounted for exactly once, normalized to TWELVE nodes. No splits, no merges, no replacements, no local variants. KY-CERT -> ky_expungement_certification (supporting action, official_pdf_fill, AOC-RU-009); KY-MISD -> ky_misdemeanor_expungement (relief track, official_pdf_fill, AOC-496.2); KY-FEL -> ky_felony_vacatur_expungement (relief track, official_pdf_fill, AOC-496.3); KY-PARDON -> ky_felony_expungement_after_pardon (relief track, official_pdf_fill, AOC-496.3 on the pardon branch); KY-AUTO-NC -> ky_automatic_nonconviction_expungement_verification (verification node, process_guidance); KY-NONCONV -> ky_nonconviction_expungement (relief track, official_pdf_fill, AOC-497.2); KY-VOID-CS -> ky_void_seal_controlled_substance (relief track, custom_pleading with AOC-334 tendered); KY-VOID-MJ -> ky_void_seal_marijuana_synthetic_salvia (relief track, custom_pleading with AOC-334 tendered); KY-DIVERSION -> ky_diversion_disposition_routing (routing node, process_guidance); KY-10 -> ky_juvenile_record_expungement (relief track, official_pdf_fill, AOC-JV-30); KY-11 -> ky_protective_order_record_expungement (relief track, official_pdf_fill, AOC-275.18); KY-12 -> ky_criminal_record_segregation (relief track, composed, two alternative custom-pleading units). All twelve import; none is deferred. KY-PARDON is kept separate from KY-FEL rather than merged because selecting the pardon branch switches off the enumerated-offence and Class D screens entirely, and merging would put a pardoned participant through a test that does not apply to them. One track is composed: ky_criminal_record_segregation, whose two units differ in actor, destination, submission and legal effect and either of which obtains relief on its own. Nothing else is composed. In particular ky_expungement_certification is not composed, because its mail and online routes are the same request to the same office through different channels, which is not a ground composition is available for; and ky_felony_vacatur_expungement is not composed, because the certification is its own supporting action and the post-order fee is ordinary post-filing handoff.
_officialAuthorityConfirmation: Shell retrieval of the Kentucky Court of Justice forms channel returns 403, but the browser layer retrieved every official form binary directly. Eleven official AOC form PDFs, the official statutory text of nine KRS sections from the Legislative Research Commission channel, the official AOC expungement certification process page and the official Kentucky Circuit Court Clerks' Manual (July 2026) were all read. No unofficial mirror or aggregator was used as controlling authority at any point; where the controlling review cited a commercial compilation, the official Legislative Research Commission text was read in its place. Corrections recorded with provenance. AOC-334 is Rev. 1-22, which the review left as merely current. The certification request form's official number is AOC-RU-009 Rev. 12-22, which the review gives as RU-009 and which resolves the identity of retained asset AOC-009. AOC-497 is confirmed to be the court's order rather than a petition, resolving a role mislabel in the readiness record. Three forms named in the review are unpublished by design rather than missing: AOC-496.5, AOC-497.3 and AOC-336 are clerk- or system-generated, their identities are established from the official Clerks' Manual, and none is participant-facing, so no packet identity is impaired and no mechanism is blocked. Three substantive corrections to the review. KRS 431.073 has a successor version effective 30 April 2027 which adds KRS 286.13-150 to the enumerated Class D list; the review states no future amendment exists, and the eligibility list is therefore date-parameterised with a release blocker. KRS 218A.275(12) bars void-and-seal relief to anyone who previously completed a KRS 218A.14151 deferred prosecution; the review does not record it and it changes who is offered a packet, so it is carried as a build blocker on that track. KRS 17.142 contains two participant-initiated routes, which is why KY-12 is normalized as a buildable track rather than left as the review's non-product classification, subject to counsel ratification. Two of the review's own build blockers are reclassified as release blockers because neither changes what is built: the AOC-497.2 checkbox completion question, where the form's own instruction is to check all that apply, the five items describe mutually exclusive dispositions and the Clerks' Manual states the conditions disjunctively; and the dismissed-diverted prejudice question, where the routing node reads the face of the order and escalates on silence. Two of the review's release blockers are closed on primary authority: the KRS 218A.276 text, unamended since 2012, and the certification requirement on the pardon basis, which KRS 431.079(1) imposes on every conviction application without a pardon carve-out.

tracks.legalName: Expungement Certification Request to the Administrative Office of the Courts (KRS 431.079)
tracks.publicName: Get the certification you need before asking to clear a conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: Every petition or application seeking expungement of a conviction must include a certification of eligibility issued by the Administrative Office of the Courts. The participant requests it on the AOC Records Unit form, pays the statutory fee, and the AOC produces the certification after a Kentucky State Police records check. The certification is an evidentiary attachment: it decides nothing, and an adverse certification does not stop the clerk from accepting a petition.

exclusions: Not required for a non-conviction petition under KRS 431.076. The Clerks' Manual states the certification requirement applies to conviction expungements.
Not required for void-and-seal relief under KRS 218A.275 or KRS 218A.276.
Not required for juvenile expungement under KRS 610.330.
Not required for protective-order record expungement under KRS 403.745 or KRS 456.070.

tracks.legalName: Petition for Expungement of a Misdemeanor, Violation or Traffic Infraction Conviction (KRS 431.078)
tracks.publicName: Clear a Kentucky misdemeanor, violation or traffic conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: On petition, the court expunges a misdemeanor, violation or traffic infraction conviction, together with any misdemeanor, violation or traffic charges dismissed or amended in the same criminal action, five years after the later of sentence completion or successful completion of probation. Relief is mandatory for a single offence or a series arising from a single incident and discretionary for a series that did not. Once expunged the proceedings are deemed never to have occurred and the participant need not disclose them.

exclusions: A sex offence, or an offence committed against a child.
An offence subject to enhancement for a second or subsequent offence, unless the enhancement window has expired.
Any felony or misdemeanor conviction in the five years before filing.
Any felony or misdemeanor proceeding pending or being instituted against the participant.
Offences against a jurisdiction other than the Commonwealth of Kentucky. KRS 431.078(10) confines the relief to Kentucky offences.

tracks.legalName: Application to Vacate and Expunge a Class D Felony Conviction (KRS 431.073)
tracks.publicName: Ask the court to vacate and clear a Kentucky Class D felony

controllingAuthority.summary: On a verified application filed in the original criminal case, the court may vacate an eligible Class D felony conviction, dismiss the charges with prejudice and order the record expunged. Relief is discretionary. The record is expunged only on full payment of the $250 expungement fee, which may be paid in instalments under KRS 534.020. Vacatur does not revive an expired limitations period, is not a finding of legal error or innocence, and does not nullify findings of fact or law.

exclusions: Class A, B and C felonies, and any felony not within KRS 431.073(1).

For the KRS 431.073(1)(d) branch: KRS 189A.010 impaired driving, KRS 508.032, KRS 519.055, abuse of public office, sex offences, offences against a child, and any offence that resulted in serious bodily injury or death.
Any conviction in the five years before the application.
Any felony or misdemeanor proceeding pending or being instituted against the applicant.

rules.postFilingInstructions: Track the prosecutor's 60-day response period from service, any extension and the statutory 120-day provisions. controllingAuthority.summary: Where a person is acquitted, or an order dismisses with prejudice all criminal charges in a case and the dismissal was not in exchange for a guilty plea to another charge, the court enters an order of automatic expungement thirty days after the judgment becomes final. The statute states that the order shall not require any action by the person. All criminal records in the custody of the court and of any other agency, including law enforcement records, are expunged and the proceedings are deemed never to have occurred. KRS 431.076(8) makes the section retroactive except for subsection (1)(a), so the automatic route does not reach dispositions before 15 July 2020.

exclusions: Dispositions before 15 July 2020, which KRS 431.076(8) excludes from the automatic subsection.
Any dismissal in exchange for a guilty plea to another offence.
Traffic infractions not otherwise classified as misdemeanors.
Cases where fewer than all charges were resolved this way. The statute reaches an order dismissing all criminal charges in a case.
Cabinet for Health and Family Services records, which KRS 431.076(4) does not reach.

Standard distribution is to the defendant or their attorney, the county or Commonwealth's attorney, the Kentucky State Police, the arresting agency, the local jail and the local pretrial office; any other agency must be asked for within sixty days of the expungement.

components.notes: Explains the 15 July 2020 boundary, the thirty-day timing, the all-charges and not-in-exchange-for-a-plea gates, and that nothing is filed and no fee is paid. Tells the participant to confirm with the circuit court clerk that AOC-497.3 was entered rather than assume it, and to ask within sixty days if an agency outside the standard distribution list needs a copy. Where no order issued, routes to ky_nonconviction_expungement.

controllingAuthority.summary: Where a protective-order petition did not result in the issuance of a domestic violence order or a non-temporary interpersonal protective order and the case was dismissed, the court may for good cause shown order expunged all records in the case in the custody of the court and any such records, including law enforcement records, in the custody of any other agency or official. The respondent moves six months after dismissal, provided no order of protection has been issued against them in the preceding six months.

exclusions: Any case in which a domestic violence order or a non-temporary interpersonal protective order was issued.
Any respondent who has been bound by, or had issued against them, an order of protection for the protection of any person in the six months before the request.
Criminal records, which this route does not reach. Those go to the criminal tracks.

tracks.legalName: Segregation of Arrest Records After Acquittal, Dismissal or Withdrawal of Charges (KRS 17.142)
tracks.publicName: Ask agencies to file away the record of an arrest that went nowhere

controllingAuthority.summary: A law enforcement or other public agency holding arrest records, fingerprints, photographs or other data must, on the written request of the arrestee, segregate those records into a file separate from those of convicted persons where the person was found innocent or all charges relating to the offence were dismissed or withdrawn. The person may instead apply to the court, which shall forthwith issue an order to all law enforcement agencies. Each agency must notify every agency it shared the records with, and the segregated record must show the disposition. Records subject to KRS 431.076 or KRS 431.078 are sealed under those statutes instead.

exclusions: Records subject to KRS 431.076 or KRS 431.078, which KRS 17.142(4) directs be sealed under those statutes instead. In practice this is most acquittals and dismissals, so segregation is a fallback.
Court records, which the Clerks' Manual records are not records that may be segregated.
Cases where fewer than all charges relating to the offence were dismissed or withdrawn.

waitingPeriods.condition: Acquittal, or dismissal or withdrawal of all charges relating to the offence

units.label: Apply to the court for an order of segregation
units.description: An application under KRS 17.142(2) to the court in which the case was tried, or would have been tried had charges been filed. On receipt the court shall forthwith issue an order to all law enforcement agencies, so one filing reaches every agency at once and carries the KRS 17.142(3) duty on each agency to notify everyone it passed the records to. No official form exists, so the application is drafted.

units.label: Send a written request to each agency holding the records
units.description: Written requests under KRS 17.142(1) addressed directly to each law enforcement or other public agency holding the records. The statutory duty to segregate runs to the agency on the arrestee's written request without any court involvement. One letter is generated per agency the participant identifies.

geography.venue: For the court application, the court in which the case was tried, or in which it would have been tried had charges been filed. For the written requests, no venue: they go to the agencies.

destination.name: The trial court on the application route, and each record-holding agency on the written-request route
destination.detail: The court application is filed with the circuit court clerk in the county of the case and produces an order binding all law enforcement agencies. The written requests are posted by the participant to each agency they identify. The two routes are independent: either obtains segregation, and a participant may use both.

components.conditionDescription: Applies on the court application unit.
components.notes: Application for Segregation of Records under KRS 17.142(2), generated from the participant's answers and filed in the court where the case was or would have been tried. No official form exists for this relief.

components.conditionDescription: Applies on the written-request unit, one letter per agency identified.
components.notes: Written request under KRS 17.142(1) to a named agency, reciting the arrest, the disposition and the statutory duty and asking the agency to segregate its records and notify the agencies it shared them with.

Explains that KRS 17.142(4) sends most acquittals and dismissals to KRS 431.076 or KRS 431.078 instead, that segregation is materially weaker than expungement because the records continue to exist and remain accessible, and that court records cannot be segregated at all. Routes to the expungement tracks first and reaches this route only as a fallback, most obviously for charges that were withdrawn.

unresolvedQuestions.question: The controlling review classifies this slot as an agency-level mechanism retained for completeness and expressly not a product track, and supplies no output strategy, filing actor or destination. The current official text of KRS 17.142 contains two participant-initiated routes, one of which is a court application on which relief is mandatory, so the product rule points the other way. Normalizing it as a buildable relief track is a departure from the review and must be ratified by counsel before anything is built.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Two participant-facing submissions exist on the face of KRS 17.142 and neither is served by an official form, so custom pleading is the vehicle for both. They are composed rather than collapsed because they differ in actor, destination, submission and legal effect: the court route produces a mandatory order binding every law enforcement agency and triggering a downstream notification duty, while the agency route engages one agency's own statutory duty directly. Either obtains relief independently, which is what makes them alternatives rather than stages. Nothing is built until counsel ratifies the departure from the review's classification.
